content.title: About
content.content: A doughnut is a piece of fried or baked dough, often glazed, dusted with powdered sugar, or filled with jam, cream, or other fillings. This entry refers to the cake‑type doughnut finished with a coating of powdered sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Doughnuts appeared in Europe in the 17th century and quickly became popular in the United States.
The classic American doughnut is ring‑shaped with a hole in the middle.
In Russia, “ponchiks” without a hole are common and are often served with jam or condensed milk.
Powdered sugar not only decorates but also creates a light, crisp crust.
In Japan, “dorayaki” style doughnuts are covered with sweet glaze and sprinkles.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Doughnuts provide a quick boost of energy thanks to their carbohydrate content, making them a convenient snack.

items.title: Carbohydrate source
items.content: The dough is rich in starch, which is easily digested and absorbed.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and yeast used in the batter contain small amounts of vitamins B1, B2 and B6.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: In modest amounts doughnuts supply iron, magnesium and phosphorus.

items.title: Powdered sugar as quick glucose
items.content: Powdered sugar can rapidly raise blood glucose, which may be helpful in cases of hypoglycemia.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Trans and saturated fats
items.content: Deep‑frying creates trans fats that are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The batter usually contains wheat, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Doughnuts are calorie‑dense; moderate consumption is advised for those monitoring their weight.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Doughnuts can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert, paired with coffee or tea, added to ice cream, or used as a base for layered cakes topped with powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store doughnuts in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator, or freeze for up to 2 months.
